## Data Context and Research Question {-}


For the spatial mini-project, you will work with data about Hennipen and Ramsey Counties, the larger geo-political districts where Macalester College is located. 

In particular, I've gathered aggregate summaries of the people who live in Hennipen or Ramsey counties, summarized for each census tract based on data from 2020 5-year average American Community Service run by the U.S. Census Bureau. A census tract is a statistical subdivision of a county that aims to have roughly 4,000 inhabitants and they are intended to be fairly homogeneous with respect to demographic and economic conditions. 

I used the `tidycensus` package to gather this data and I've provided example code in the cleaning file for how I collected the data. 

Make sure to look at a Google Map of Hennipen and Ramsey Counties, so you can familiarize yourself with the geography, <https://goo.gl/maps/m9pXVtjisoZHTmFL7>.

In particular, I want you to **focus on home values for this mini-project**.

## OLS Model {-}

7. Fit a linear model with `lm()` to address the research question above and then map the residuals by coloring the spatial polygons by the residuals. Comment on what you learn.

ANSWER:


```{r}

lm_mod <- lm(? ~ ?, data = tc_data)

tc_data$lm_resid <- resid(lm_mod)

tc_data %>% ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = lm_resid)) +
  labs(fill = 'Residuals') + 
  scale_fill_gradient2(mid = "white", high = "red", low = "blue") + theme_classic()
```

## Spatial Correlation {-}

8. Let's calculate and visualize the spatial correlation of the residuals using Global and Local Moran's I. Comment on the strength of spatial correlation based on the Global Moran's I and whether it is discernibly different from 0 (independence) and patterns in the Local Moran's I.

ANSWER:

```{r}
W <- nb2listw(Queen, style = "W") #style = 'W' gives row-normalized weights
mp <- spdep::moran.plot(tc_data$lm_resid, W, plot=FALSE)

ggplot(mp, aes(x = x, y = wx)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method="lm" , se = FALSE) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(mp$wx), lty=2) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(mp$x), lty=2) + theme_classic() + 
  labs(x = 'Residuals',y = "Average Residual of Neighbors", title = "Spatial Autocorrelation of Residuals")

local_moran <- spdep::localmoran(tc_data$lm_resid, W)

tc_data %>% bind_cols(local_moran) %>% 
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = Ii)) +
  labs(fill = 'Local Moran I') + 
  scale_fill_gradient2(mid = "white", high = "red", low = "blue") + theme_classic()

tc_data %>% bind_cols(local_moran) %>% bind_cols(attr(local_moran,'quadr')) %>%
  mutate(mean = if_else(`Pr(z != E(Ii))` < 0.005, mean,NA)) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = mean)) +
  labs(fill = 'Local Moran I Hotspots') + 
  scale_fill_manual(values=c('red'),na.value = 'lightgrey' ) + theme_classic()


W <- nb2listw(Queen, style = "B") #style = 'B' gives binary weights
spdep::moran.test(tc_data$lm_resid, W, alternative = "two.sided", randomisation = TRUE)  # Global Moran's I, using randomization test

```
